post.description: Starts a process in a ready sandbox (a creating or starting one is awaited up to 60 s). Exactly one of `command` (bash -lc) and `argv`. Modes: `sync` (default) answers 200 SyncCommandResult once the process exits (timeout at most 600 s; the connection is silent until then, so proxies may cut it: SDKs use stream); `stream` answers 200 application/x-ndjson frames (first `started`, last `exit`, `reconnect` or `error`) with `Sbx-Command-Id`; `detached` answers 201 Command right after the start. With an Idempotency-Key a repeat never starts the command twice: sync waits for the same command, stream streams it from offset 0 with `started.replayed: true`, detached answers 200.

put.description: Unpacks the streamed body (tar, or tar.gz with format=tar.gz) into the directory `path`. Owner is `user`; uid/gid of the archive are ignored, setuid/setgid dropped. Limits: 200 000 entries, 16 GiB of data, 4 096-byte paths, else 413. Absolute paths, `..`, hard links out of the archive, devices and FIFOs, and writing through a symlink (from the archive or already on disk) are 400 invalid_path. Not atomic: on an error what was written stays (details.entriesWritten); unpack into a new directory and move it for atomicity. Not resumable: repeat the whole archive (safe with overwrite=true).

post.description: Starts a resumable upload of a large file. Nothing is stored by the api; the partial file lives in the sandbox and is dropped after 24 h without activity. Flow: POST .../uploads {path} → PUT .../uploads/{upload}?offset=N&path= (chunks up to 8 MiB, offset = bytes so far) → POST .../uploads/{upload}/commit {path, sha256}. After a break, HEAD .../uploads/{upload} gives Sbx-Upload-Offset to resume from. A chunk whose offset is not the current size is 409 upload_offset_mismatch with the current offset (header Sbx-Upload-Offset, details.offset): continue from there.

post.description: Starts a PTY command in a ready sandbox (a creating or starting one is awaited up to 60 s): the user's login shell, or `command` run by `bash -lc` in the terminal. Connect with GET .../connect (WebSocket), or read it with GET .../commands/{command}/stream?ptyOffset= and write with POST .../commands/{command}/input. A PTY with no client connected is closed by the agent after 10 min (reason pty_idle). With an Idempotency-Key a repeat returns the same command with 200 and `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. get.description: WebSocket upgrade with the subprotocol `sbx.pty.v1` (required). Server → client: binary frames are consecutive PTY output bytes; text frames are JSON: `{"type":"attached","offset":N}` first, `{"type":"truncated","availableFrom":N}`, `{"type":"exit",...}` (as in NDJSON), `{"type":"error","code","message","retryable","details","requestId"}`, `{"type":"reconnect","offset":N,"reason"}`. The client counts the offset itself: `attached.offset` (or `availableFrom` after truncated) plus the bytes received. Client → server: binary frames are input (a key typed while the socket drops may be lost, never applied twice); text `{"type":"resize","cols":N,"rows":N}`. Close codes: 1000 after exit; 1012 server shutdown (after `reconnect`); 4401 unauthorized; 4403 forbidden; 4404 no such PTY; 4409 sandbox not ready; 4503 agent unavailable (reconnect later); 1008 malformed control frame. Reconnect with `offset` = your count; `tailBytes` for scrollback. Pings every 15 s. Authentication as for other requests; in the browser (dashboard origin) the session, with `Origin` checked and `?team=` instead of the Sbx-Team header.
